'''Difficulties''' are settings that adjust the game's overall experience. In general, it affects the color, stats and quantity of [[Creatures|enemies]], the overall quality of loot and the amount of experience points heroes earn.

Players who are new to ''[[Dungeon Defenders]]'' should first play through the [[Maps|Classic Campaign]] on Easy, Medium or Hard, then work their way up. Insane and above have additional changes beyond improving enemy stats and rewards.

== Insane ==
* [[Eternia Crystal|Eternia Crystals]] do not heal between waves. They still get healed prior to a boss fight, but not on some [[The Lost Quests|Lost Quest]] maps.
* The following two changes do not apply to [[Survival Mode]] or [[Pure Strategy]]:
** Each Build Phase is on a forced timer before the next Combat Phase starts automatically.
**''[[Hero Casting Rate]]'' is not increased during Build Phases.

=== Insane+ ( Console Only ) ===
Main Article: [[INSANE+ (Console Only)|Insane+ Difficulty]]

The difference between Insane & '''Insane+''' are way greater compared to the jump from Hard to Insane difficulty. Nightmare enemies do not spawn on this difficulty level at all.

* Enemies gain a large health buff, damage buff, give x2.5 more score when defeated.
* Crystal's get double the health, ( Enemy Crystals are not affected).
* Player health / damage / resistances are not affected or decreased & projectile speed is not affected.
* Defenses do not gain any multipliers to their health or damage.
* Tavern keeper gives a x2.5 score multiplier when the exp bonus is bought.
* Time bonus and wave completion scores get a x2.5 multiplier on them.
* Loot quality is increased & tavern keeper shop items quality increased, this also applies to wave 15 / 25 pet awards & challenge awards.
* Contains a lot of the gameplay changes that are in regular Insane difficulty.

== Nightmare (NM) ==
''Main Article: [[Nightmare (Difficulty)]]''

The differences between Insane and '''Nightmare''' are far greater than Hard vs. Insane. [[Ogre|Ogres]] are significantly more common. [[Spider|Spiders]], [[Djinn]] and [[Sharken]] will spawn on almost all maps. [[Goblin Copter|Goblin Copters]] spawn on most maps that have [[Wyvern|Wyverns]]. Nightmare also modifies the stats of [[heroes]], [[pets]] and [[defenses]]. Below are a few notable examples:

* Hero [[weapons]] and [[abilities]] deal less damage, but pets and defenses hit harder than usual.
* All heroes, physical defenses and [[Eternia Crystal|Eternia Crystals]] have their maximum health scaled up. The potency of [[Healing Aura|Healing Auras]] and health-restoring pets (barring [[Mage Minion|Mage Minions]] whose healing is already percent-based) is increased to account for this.
* [[Damage Resistance|Damage Resistances]] from equipment are reduced by 0.55x; a sum of 164% is now required in order to reach the 90% cap per damage type.
* [[Auras]] have 15% shorter lifespans and 30% less range. The potencies for [[Ensnare Aura|Ensnare]], [[Strength Drain Aura|Strength Drain]] and [[Enrage Aura|Enrage Auras]] are nerfed by a factor of 0.75x. More ''Aura Effect Strength'' and/or damage buffs is/are needed the reach the Ensnare and Enrage caps and return Strength Drains to respectable levels (around 0.25x enemy damage after [[Upgrade Defense|upgrades]] to it and a touching [[Tower Buff Beam|buff beam]]).

Insane+ is the Nightmare equivalent on console versions with different mechanics.

'''Ruthless''' was introduced in Patch 9.5.0.

== Ascension ([[Redux]] Exclusive) ==
''Main Article: [[Ascension (Difficulty)]]''

'''Ascension''' is an even higher difficulty level introduced in ''[[Dungeon Defenders Redux]]''. It makes a variety of missions on-par with endgame progression, building off of the Final Update to the Vanilla PC game in November 2019. Many missions on this difficulty feature [[Cyclops|Cyclopes]], a terracotta-colored [[Ogre]] variant that tosses snot bubbles instead of opaque balls. The lingering damage overtime on impact can be deadly to [[heroes]] and [[Summoner|summoned minions]].

Unlike Nightmare, Ascension mostly applies balance changes to how certain boss fights and [[challenges]] play out, rather than altering heroes and defenses directly. For example:

* The 20 [[Series EV|Series EVs]] fought during the [[Lab Assault]] challenge will teleport if they fall off the map. This prevents players from exploiting their AI to an easy victory.
* The last two waves of [[Raining Goblins]] feature [[Harbinger (Creature)|Harbingers]]. The [[Goblin|Goblins]] and [[Orc|Orcs]] are also immune to [[Gas Trap|Gas Traps]], regardless of [[Elements|elemental affinity]].
* In assault challenges, pets that heal heroes restore far less HP at a time.
